Midnight Office For Use at Home
Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us! Amen! Glory to Thee, O God, glory to Thee! O Heavenly King, Comforter, Spirit of Truth, who art everywhere present and fillest all things, Treasury of good things and Giver of life: Come and abide in us, and cleanse us from every stain, and save our souls, O Good One! (From Pascha until Pentecost, “O Heavenly King” is not said;
from Pascha to its Leavetaking, “Christ is risen” is said three times in its place.) Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us! (3x) Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen. All-holy Trinity, have mercy on us. Lord, cleanse us from our sins. Master, pardon our transgressions. Holy One, look upon and heal our infirmities for Thy name’s sake. Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen. Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors, and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. Amen. Lord, have mercy (12).
Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen. Come, let us worship God our King Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ, our King and our God. Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ Himself, our King and our God.
Psalm 50
Have mercy on me, O God, according to thy great mercy, and according to the multitude of thy compassions, blot out my transgressions. Wash me yet more from my transgressions, and from my sin purify thou me. For I know my transgression, and my sin is continually before me. Against thee alone have I sinned, and have done evil before thee; that thou mightest be justified in thy words, and conquer when thou art judged.
Behold, in transgressions was I conceived, and in sin did my mother bear me. Behold, thou hast loved truth; the hidden and secret things of thy wisdom hast thou revealed unto me. Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; thou shalt wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow. Thou shalt make me hear joy and gladness; the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice. Turn away thy face from my sins, and blot out my transgressions.
Create in me a clean heart, and renew a right spirit within me. Cast me not away from thy face, and take not thy Holy Spirit from me. Give me again the joy of thy salvation, and establish me with a princely spirit. Then will I teach transgressors thy ways, and the impious shall return unto thee. Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, the God of my salvation; my tongue shall rejoice in thy righteousness. O Lord, open thou my lips, and my mouth shall declare thy praise.
For if thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would have given it; with burnt-offerings thou wilt not be pleased. A sacrifice to God is a broken spirit; a broken and humbled heart God will not despise. Do good, O Lord, in thy goodwill unto Zion; and let the walls of Jerusalem be built. Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifice of righteousness, oblations, and burnt- offerings; then shall they lay bullocks upon thine altar.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
Here we may insert hymns from the Octoechos/Triodion
Then on weekdays, we may read the Seventeenth Kathisma (Psalm 118/119).
After the kathisma (if we read one), we say: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
The Creed
I believe in one God, the Father almighty, Maker of Heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord, Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Only-begotten, begotten of the Father before all ages; Light of Light, true God of true God; begotten, not made; of one essence with the Father; by whom all things were made. Who for us men and our salvation came down from heaven, and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary, and became man.
And was crucified also for us under Pontius Pilate, and suffered and was buried; and the third day He rose again according to the Scriptures; and ascended into heaven and sitteth at the right hand of the Father. And He shall come again with glory to judge the living and the dead; of His kingdom there shall be no end.
And in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the Giver of life, who proceedeth from the Father, who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified, who spake by the prophets. In one holy, catholic, and apostolic Church; I confess one baptism for the forgiveness of sins; I look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the age to come. Amen.
Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us! (3x) Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen. All-holy Trinity, have mercy on us. Lord, cleanse us from our sins. Master, pardon our transgressions. Holy One, look upon and heal our infirmities for Thy name’s sake. Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen. Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors, and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. Amen.
Then these troparia in tone 8:
Behold, the Bridegroom cometh at midnight, and blessed is the servant whom He shall find watchful, but again unworthy is he whom He shall find slothful. Beware, then, O my soul, let by sleep thou be weighed down, and be given over unto death and shut thyself out from the kingdom; but awake crying: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God; through the Theotokos, have mercy on us.
Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
While meditating on that fearful day, O my soul, be watchful, kindling thy lamp, lighting it with oil, for thou knowest not when the voice shall come unto thee, saying: “Behold, the Bridegroom.” Beware then, O my soul, lest thou slumber and remain knocking without, like the five virgins
Both now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
We pray thee, O Virgin Theotokos, thou impregnable wall, bulwark of salvation, frustrate the counsel of the adversary, the sorrows of thy people change into joy, recall thy world and strengthen the pious; intercede for the peace of the world, O Theotokos, for thou art our hope. Lord, have mercy.
(40) O Thou, who at all times and at every hour, both in heaven and on earth, art worshipped and glorified, O Christ God, long-suffering, great in mercy and goodness of heart, who lovest the righteous and hast mercy on sinners, who callest all men to salvation through the tidings of good things to come: do Thou, the same Lord, receive also our prayers at this hour;
direct our lives in thy commandments, sanctify our souls, cleanse our bodies, direct our thoughts, cleanse our minds, and deliver us from every tribulation, wickedness, and affliction; encompass us by Thy holy angels, that guarded and guided by their host, we may attain to the unity of the faith, and to the understanding of Thine unapproachable glory, for blessed art thou uunto ages of ages. Amen. Lord, have mercy.
(3) Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen. More honorable than the Cherubim and more glorious without compare than the Seraphim, who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word: verily, Theotokos, we magnify thee. Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ have mercy on us. Amen. During the Great Fast, (when the Alleluia is sung), the prayer of St. Ephrem of Syria is read now.
O Lord and Master of my life, the spirit of idleness, of despondency, of love of power, and of idle words, grant me not. (Prostration) But the spirit of continence, of humility, of patience, and of love, do Thou grant unto me Thy servant. (Prostration) Yea O Lord and King, grant unto me to perceive mine own offences and not to judge my brother; for blessed art Thou uunto ages of ages. Amen. (Prostration)
Then 12 bows to the waist while saying:
O God, cleanse Thou me a sinner and have mercy on me (12).
OR
O God, have mercy on me a sinner (3). O God, cleanse Thou me a sinner and have mercy on me (3). Thou hast created me, O Lord, have mercy on me (3). Countless times have I sinned, O Lord, forgive me. (3)
Then repeat the prayer in full, and conclude with a prostration.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
The prayer of St. Mardarius
O Master, God, Father Almighty, Lord, Only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Spirit, one Godhead, one Power: have mercy on me a sinner, and, by the judgements which Thou discernest, save me Thine unworthy servant, for blessed art thou unto ages of ages. Amen.
A Prayer of St. Basil the Great
Almighty Lord, the God of hosts and of all flesh, who livest in the heights, yet lookest down on the humble, proving the hearts and emotions, clearly foreknowing the secrets of men: Thou art the Light without beginning, in Whom there is no variation nor shadow of change. O Immortal King, accept the prayers which we now offer Thee from defiled lips. Free us from the sins we have committed in deed, word or thought, knowingly and unknowingly.
Cleanse us from all defilement of flesh and spirit. Grant us to pass through the entire night of this present life with a watchful heart and a sober mind, awaiting the coming of the bright and manifest day of Thine only-begotten Son, our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, when the Judge of all will come with glory to reward each according to his deeds.
May we not be found fallen and lazy, but alert and roused to action, prepared to enter into His joy and the divine chamber of His glory, where the voice of those who feast is unceasing and indescribable is the delight of those who behold the inexpressible beauty of Thy countenance. For Thou art the true Light which enlightens and sanctifies all, and all creation hymns Thee uunto ages of ages. Amen
Another Prayer of St. Basil We bless Thee, most high God and Lord of mercies, Who ever doest great and unfathomable things for us – glorious and awesome things without number. Thou givest us sleep for the repose of our frailty, relieving the labors of our over-burdened flesh. We thank Thee for not destroying us in our lawlessness. Instead, Thou has shown Thy usual love for mankind, and raised us, as we lay in despair, to glorify Thy Reign.
Therefore, we implore Thy boundless goodness: enlighten our thoughts and eyes, and awaken our minds from the heavy sleep of laziness. Open our lips and fill them with Thy praise, that we may unwaveringly hymn and confess Thee, the God glorified in all and by all, Father without beginning, with Thine only-begotten Son and Thine all-holy, and life-giving Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
A Prayer of St. Eustratius
Greatly will I magnify thee, O Lord, for Thou didst look upon my humility and didst not shut me up in the hands of the enemy, but thou hast saved my soul from necessities. And now, O Master, let thy hand shelter me, and let thy mercy come upon me, for my soul is disquieted and pained at its departure from this my wretched and foul body.
May the evil counsel of the foe never meet and hinder it in the darkness because of the sins that in ignorance and with knowledge I have committed in this life. Be gracious unto me, O Mater, and let not my soul see the murky and dark vision of evil demons, but let it be received by thy radiant and shining angels. Give glory to thy holy name, and by thy power lead me to thy divine judgment seat.
When I shall be judged, let not the hand of the prince of this world take me in order to drag me, a sinner, down into the depths of hell, but stand thou near me, and be unto me a Savior and Helper. Let these bodily torments be a joy unto thy servants. Have mercy, O Lord, on my soul made foul with the passion s of this life, and receive it cleansed through repentance and confession, for blessed art thou uunto ages of ages. Amen.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
Come, let us worship God our King. Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ, our King and our God. Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ Himself, our King and our God.
Psalm 120
I lifted up mine eyes unto the mountains, whence cometh my help. My help is from the Lord, who hath made heaven and earth. Let not my foot be given to wavering, nor He that keepeth thee slumber. Behold, He that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep. The Lord shall keep thee; the Lord is thy shield upon thy right hand. By day the sun shall not smite thee, nor the moon by night. The Lord shall keep thee from all evil; the Lord shall keep thy soul.
The Lord shall keep thy coming in and thy going out henceforth and forevermore.
Psalm 133
Behold now, bless the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord, that stand in the house of the Lord, n the courts of the house of our God. In the nights lift up your hands in the sanctuaries and bless ye the Lord. May the Lord bless thee out of Zion, He that made heaven and earth.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now an ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us! (3x) Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen. All-holy Trinity, have mercy on us. Lord, cleanse us from our sins. Master, pardon our transgressions. Holy One, look upon and heal our infirmities for Thy name’s sake. Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen. Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors, and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. Amen.
These Troparia for the Departed in Tone 2
O Lord, as thou art good, remember thy servants, and pardon them in whatsoever they have sinned during their life, for none is without sin, but thou who art able to give rest to the departed.
Out of the depth of wisdom and with love of man dost thou dispense all things, and dost distribute to all that which is expedient, O only Artificer; give rest, O Lord, to the souls of they servants, for they did put their hope in thee, our Maker and our Fashioner and our God.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit. With the saints give rest, O Christ, to the souls of Thy servant(s), where there is neither sickness nor sorrow, and no more sighing, but life everlasting.
Now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion
We bless thee in every generation, O Virgin Theotokos, for in thee the uncontained Christ was well-pleased to be contained. Blessed are we also that have thee as a Protectress, for day and night, thou dost intercede for us, and the scepters of kings by thy supplications are strengthened. Wherefore in hymning thee, we cry to thee: Rejoice, O thou who art full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
Lord, have mercy (12).
And these prayers:
The Remembrancer Remember, O Lord, our fathers and brethren who have fallen asleep in the hope of the resurrection unto life eternal, and all them that in piety and faith have completed their lives.
Pardon every sin committed by them in word or deed or thought, and settle them in a place of light, in a place of verdure, in a place of repose, whence all sickness, sorrow, and sighing have fled away, where the light of thy face watcheth over and gladdeneth all thy Saints from the ages. Grant them and us thy kingdom and participation in thine endless and blessed life.
For thou art the Resurrection, and the Life, and the Repose of thy servants who have fallen asleep, O Christ our God, and unto thee do we send up glory, together with thy Father, who is without beginning, and thine all-holy, and good, and life-creating Spirit, not and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
O most glorious ever-virgin Mother of Christ God, offer our prayers unto thy Son and our God, that He may, through thee, save our souls.
All my hope I place on thee, O Mother of God; keep me beneath thy shelter.
My hope is the Father, my refuge is the Son, my protection is the Holy Spirit; O Holy Trinity, glory to thee.
And these Troparia in tone 6:
Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us, for laying aside all excuse, we sinners offer unto Thee as to our Master, this supplication: have mercy on us.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. O Lord, have mercy on us, for in Thee have put our hope. Do not be angry with us, neither remember our iniquities, but look down on us even now, since Thou art compassionate, and deliver us from our enemies; for Thou art our God and we are Thy people; we are all the works of Thy hands, and we call on Thy Name.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
Now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
O Blessed Theotokos, open the doors of compassion to us whose hope is in thee, that we may not perish but be delivered from adversities, through thee who art the salvation of the Christian people.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
Lord, have mercy (3). Through the prayers of our holy fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ our God have mercy on us. Amen.

Basil's Liturgy, as the latter, in turn, was a later and abbreviated form of a
 still earlier Liturgy.
 It is appointed to be used on the Sundays of the Great Fast (Lent), except
 on Palm Sunday; on Holy Thursday and Holy Saturday; and on Christmas
 Day and the Epiphany, when those feasts fall upon Sunday or Monday ; other-
 wise, on the days preceding those feasts. Also, on St. Basil's Day, January I;
 in all, ten times in the course of the year.
 The Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts, so called because the Holy Gifts
 which have previously been consecrated are used for the Holy Communion,
 has existed from ancient times, although, in its present form, it is ascribed to
 St. Gregory Homiliastes of Rome (sixth century). The Orthodox Church de-
 crees that this Liturgy shall be celebrated during the Great Fast (but at no
 other time), since the triumphantly joyous feelings associated with the corn-
 plete Liturgy and the consecration of the Holy Gifts are incompatible with
 the strictness of the Fast. Hence it is ordained that the complete Liturgy
 shall be celebrated only on Saturdays and Sundays during the weeks of the
 Great Fast (Lent). The customary days for the celebration of the Liturgy
 of the Presanctified Gifts are Wednesday and Friday of every week, and on
 Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of Passion Week.
 The Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts consists of Vespers (and therefore is
THE DIVINE LITURGY 65
appointed for a late hour in the day), and of a portion of the ordinary Liturgy,
omitting the most essential part of the latter, namely, the consecration of the
Gifts. The Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts is usually preceded by the read-
ing of the Third, Sixth and Ninth Hours, and of the Typical Psalms. Under
certain circumstances an earlier celebration is admissible.
 The usual hour for celebrating the ordinary Liturgy is, not earlier than
dawn, and wt later than noon.
 For the celebration of the Mystery of the Eucharist the following are indis-
pensable : A Priest or a Bishop regularly ordained, and having a steadfast
will and intention to fulfil the Mystery of the Lord's Body and Blood. Of
material things : five Altar-breads, made of pure wheaten flour, and leavened ;
wine of the grape. The accomplishment of the Mystery through prayer and
words, with the blessing of the Priest's hand: "And make this bread the
precious Body of thy Christ, and also that which is in this cup the precious
 Blood of thy Christ, transmuting them by thy Holy Spirit."
 In addition to the above, the following things are indispensable for the
Liturgy : A Corporal (Antimfm),* consecrated by a Bishop ; vestments for
the Priest, consisting of a cassock (stikhdr), a stole (cpitraRhfI), gauntlets
(p6m/chz], girdle (pbynr), and chasuble w16n) ; vessels, -a chalice, a paten,
a star-cover, a spear, a spoon ; veils, a censer, a service book ; lights burning
on the altar ; and an acolyte.
 Only one Liturgy may be celebrated on any Altar in the course of one day ;
 and no Bishop or Priest may celebrate more than one Liturgy in the course
of one and the same day.
 The Priest who enters upon the celebration of the Liturgy must be free
from inhibition, and from mortal sin, and must prepare himself,- spiritually, ,
by reconciling himself with all men, by penitence, and the appointed devo-
tions ; bodily, by abstinence from food and drink(from midnight at the least),
and from fleshly desires, and'by cleanliness of body and garments.
 The appointed devotions consist of the celebration or the hearing of the
Evening and Morning Services and Prayers ; and there must also be read : .
On Monday: The Canon to the Lord Jesus, the Invocation to the Birthgiver
of God, the Canon to the Archangels; and, if he so desire, to his Guardian
Angel. On Tuesday: The Canon to the Lord Jesus, the Invocation to the
Birth-giver of God, to John the Forerunner, and to his Guardian Angel. On
Wednesday: The Canon to the Lord Jesus, the Canon to the Birth-giver of
God, and to his Guardian Angel. On Thursday: The Canon to the Lord
Jesus, the Invocation to the Birth-giver of God, to his Guardian Angel, to
the Holy Apostles ; and, if he so desire, to St. Nicholas. On Friday, the
Canon to the Life-giving Cross, the Invocation to the Birth-giver of God,
and to his Guardian Angel. On Saturday: The Canon to the Lord Jesus,
the Chant of Prayer and Praise (Akd@t) to the Birth-giver of God, to his
Guardian Angel, and to all the Saints. On Sunday : The Canon to the Lord
Jesus, the Invocation to the Birth-giver of God, and to his Guardian Angel.
 In addition to these, on every occasion, the Canon of the Communion, and
the Prayers before the Communion. (See I&.)

documents.search_text: the office of oblation complete office of oblation from the public-domain 1906 service book. basil's liturgy, as the latter, in turn, was a later and abbreviated form of a still earlier liturgy. it is appointed to be used on the sundays of the great fast (lent), except on palm sunday; on holy thursday and holy saturday; and on christmas day and the epiphany, when those feasts fall upon sunday or monday ; other- wise, on the days preceding those feasts. also, on st. basil's day, january i; in all, ten times in the course of the year. the liturgy of the presanctified gifts, so called because the holy gifts which have previously been consecrated are used for the holy communion, has existed from ancient times, although, in its present form, it is ascribed to st. gregory homiliastes of rome (sixth century). the orthodox church de- crees that this liturgy shall be celebrated during the great fast (but at no other time), since the triumphantly joyous feelings associated with the corn- plete liturgy and the consecration of the holy gifts are incompatible with the strictness of the fast. hence it is ordained that the complete liturgy shall be celebrated only on saturdays and sundays during the weeks of the great fast (lent). the customary days for the celebration of the liturgy of the presanctified gifts are wednesday and friday of every week, and on monday, tuesday and wednesday of passion week. the liturgy of the presanctified gifts consists of vespers (and therefore is the divine liturgy 65 appointed for a late hour in the day), and of a portion of the ordinary liturgy, omitting the most essential part of the latter, namely, the consecration of the gifts. the liturgy of the presanctified gifts is usually preceded by the read- ing of the third, sixth and ninth hours, and of the typical psalms. under certain circumstances an earlier celebration is admissible. the usual hour for celebrating the ordinary liturgy is, not earlier than dawn, and wt later than noon. for the celebration of the mystery of the eucharist the following are indis- pensable : a priest or a bishop regularly ordained, and having a steadfast will and intention to fulfil the mystery of the lord's body and blood. of material things : five altar-breads, made of pure wheaten flour, and leavened ; wine of the grape. the accomplishment of the mystery through prayer and words, with the blessing of the priest's hand: "and make this bread the precious body of thy christ, and also that which is in this cup the precious blood of thy christ, transmuting them by thy holy spirit." in addition to the above, the following things are indispensable for the liturgy : a corporal (antimfm),* consecrated by a bishop ; vestments for the priest, consisting of a cassock (stikhdr), a stole (cpitrarhfi), gauntlets (p6m/chz], girdle (pbynr), and chasuble w16n) ; vessels, -a chalice, a paten, a star-cover, a spear, a spoon ; veils, a censer, a service book ; lights burning on the altar ; and an acolyte. only one liturgy may be celebrated on any altar in the course of one day ; and no bishop or priest may celebrate more than one liturgy in the course of one and the same day. the priest who enters upon the celebration of the liturgy must be free from inhibition, and from mortal sin, and must prepare himself,- spiritually, , by reconciling himself with all men, by penitence, and the appointed devo- tions ; bodily, by abstinence from food and drink(from midnight at the least), and from fleshly desires, and'by cleanliness of body and garments. the appointed devotions consist of the celebration or the hearing of the evening and morning services and prayers ; and there must also be read : . on monday: the canon to the lord jesus, the invocation to the birthgiver of god, the canon to the archangels; and, if he so desire, to his guardian angel. on tuesday: the canon to the lord jesus, the invocation to the birth-giver of god, to john the forerunner, and to his guardian angel. on wednesday: the canon to the lord jesus, the canon to the birth-giver of god, and to his guardian angel. on thursday: the canon to the lord jesus, the invocation to the birth-giver of god, to his guardian angel, to the holy apostles ; summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:16

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:16

text.en: Otherwise, if you bless with the spirit, how will he who fills the place of the unlearned say the “Amen” at your giving of thanks, seeing he doesn’t know what you say?

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:17

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:17

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:17

text.en: For you most certainly give thanks well, but the other person is not built up.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:18

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:18

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:18

text.en: I thank my God, I speak with other languages more than you all.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:19

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:19

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:19

text.en: However, in the assembly I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others also, than ten thousand words in another language.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:26

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:26

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:26

text.en: What is it then, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has another language, or has an interpretation. Let all things be done to build each other up.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:27

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:27

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:27

text.en: If any man speaks in another language, let there be two, or at the most three, and in turn; and let one interpret.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:28

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:28

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:28

text.en: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the assembly, and let him speak to himself and to God.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:29

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:29

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:29

text.en: Let two or three of the prophets speak, and let the others discern.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:30

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:30

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:30

text.en: But if a revelation is made to another sitting by, let the first keep silent.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:31

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:31

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:31

text.en: For you all can prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be exhorted.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:32

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:32

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:32

text.en: The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:33

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:33

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:33

text.en: for God is not a God of confusion but of peace, as in all the assemblies of the saints.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:34

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:34

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:34

text.en: Let the wives be quiet in the assemblies, for it has not been permitted for them to be talking except in submission, as the law also says,

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:35

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:35

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:35

text.en: if they desire to learn anything. “Let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a wife to be talking in the assembly.”

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:36

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:36

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:36

text.en: What!? Was it from you that the word of God went out? Or did it come to you alone?

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:37

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:37

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:37

text.en: If any man thinks himself to be a prophet or spiritual, let him recognize the things which I write to you, that they are the commandment of the Lord.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:38

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:38

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:38

text.en: But if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:39

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:39

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:39

text.en: Therefore, brothers, desire earnestly to prophesy, and don’t forbid speaking with other languages.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 14:40

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 14:40

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 14:40

text.en: Let all things be done decently and in order.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:12

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:12

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:12

text.en: Now if Christ is preached, that he has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:13

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:13

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:13

text.en: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:14

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:14

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:14

text.en: If Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith also is in vain.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:15

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:15

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:15

text.en: Yes, we are also found false witnesses of God, because we testified about God that he raised up Christ, whom he didn’t raise up if it is true that the dead are not raised.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:16

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:16

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:16

text.en: For if the dead aren’t raised, neither has Christ been raised.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:17

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:17

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:17

text.en: If Christ has not been raised, your faith is vain; you are still in your sins.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:18

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:18

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:18

text.en: Then they also who are fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:19

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:19

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:19

text.en: If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, we are of all men most pitiable.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:29

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:29

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:29

text.en: Or else what will they do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead aren’t raised at all, why then are they baptized for the dead?

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:30

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:30

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:30

text.en: Why do we also stand in jeopardy every hour?

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:31

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:31

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:31

text.en: I affirm, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:32

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:32

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:32

text.en: If I fought with animals at Ephesus for human purposes, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, then “let’s eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:33

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:33

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:33

text.en: Don’t be deceived! “Evil companionships corrupt good morals.”

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:34

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:34

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:34

text.en: Wake up righteously and don’t sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:35

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:35

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:35

text.en: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised?” and, “With what kind of body do they come?”

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:36

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:36

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:36

text.en: You foolish one, that which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:37

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:37

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:37

text.en: That which you sow, you don’t sow the body that will be, but a bare grain, maybe of wheat, or of some other kind.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 15:38

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 15:38

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 15:38

text.en: But God gives it a body even as it pleased him, and to each seed a body of its own.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 16:4

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 16:4

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 16:4

text.en: If it is appropriate for me to go also, they will go with me.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 16:5

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 16:5

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 16:5

text.en: I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 16:6

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 16:6

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 16:6

text.en: But with you it may be that I will stay with you, or even winter with you, that you may send me on my journey wherever I go.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 16:7

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 16:7

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 16:7

text.en: For I do not wish to see you now in passing, but I hope to stay a while with you, if the Lord permits.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 16:8

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 16:8

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 16:8

text.en: But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost,

title.en: 1 Corinthians 16:9

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 16:9

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 16:9

text.en: for a great and effective door has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 16:10

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 16:10

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 16:10

text.en: Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 16:11

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 16:11

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 16:11

text.en: Therefore let no one despise him. But set him forward on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I expect him with the brothers.

title.en: 1 Corinthians 16:12

summary.en: 1 Corinthians 16:12

speaker.en: 1 Corinthians 16:12

text.en: Now concerning Apollos the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, but it was not at all his desire to come now; but he will come when he has an opportunity.

title.en: 2 Corinthians 1:1

summary.en: 2 Corinthians 1:1

speaker.en: 2 Corinthians 1:1

text.en: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the assembly of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are in the whole of Achaia:

title.en: 2 Corinthians 1:2

summary.en: 2 Corinthians 1:2

speaker.en: 2 Corinthians 1:2

text.en: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

title.en: 2 Corinthians 1:3

summary.en: 2 Corinthians 1:3

speaker.en: 2 Corinthians 1:3

text.en: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort,

title.en: 2 Corinthians 1:4

summary.en: 2 Corinthians 1:4

speaker.en: 2 Corinthians 1:4

text.en: who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.

title.en: 2 Corinthians 1:5

summary.en: 2 Corinthians 1:5

speaker.en: 2 Corinthians 1:5

text.en: For as the sufferings of Christ abound to us, even so our comfort also abounds through Christ.

title.en: 2 Corinthians 1:6

summary.en: 2 Corinthians 1:6

speaker.en: 2 Corinthians 1:6

text.en: But if we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which produces in you the patient enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer.

title.en: 2 Corinthians 1:7

summary.en: 2 Corinthians 1:7

speaker.en: 2 Corinthians 1:7

text.en: Our hope for you is steadfast, knowing that, since you are partakers of the sufferings, so you are also of the comfort.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:12

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:12

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:12

text.en: For our boasting is this: the testimony of our conscience that in holiness and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God, we behaved ourselves in the world, and more abundantly toward you.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:13

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:13

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:13

text.en: For we write no other things to you than what you read or even acknowledge, and I hope you will acknowledge to the end—

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:14

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:14

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:14

text.en: as also you acknowledged us in part—that we are your boasting, even as you also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:15

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:15

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:15

text.en: In this confidence, I was determined to come first to you, that you might have a second benefit,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:16

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:16

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:16

text.en: and by you to pass into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and to be sent forward by you on my journey to Judea.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:17

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:17

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:17

text.en: When I therefore planned this, did I show fickleness? Or the things that I plan, do I plan according to the flesh, that with me there should be the “Yes, yes” and the “No, no?”

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:18

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:18

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:18

text.en: But as God is faithful, our word toward you was not “Yes and no.”

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:19

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:19

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:19

text.en: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us—by me, Silvanus, and Timothy—was not “Yes and no,” but in him is “Yes.”

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:20

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:20

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 1:20

text.en: For however many are the promises of God, in him is the “Yes.” Therefore also through him is the “Amen”, to the glory of God through us.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:4

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:4

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:4

text.en: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not that you should be made to grieve, but that you might know the love that I have so abundantly for you.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:5

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:5

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:5

text.en: But if any has caused sorrow, he has caused sorrow not to me, but in part (that I not press too heavily) to you all.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:6

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:6

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:6

text.en: This punishment which was inflicted by the many is sufficient for such a one;

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:7

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:7

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:7

text.en: so that, on the contrary, you should rather forgive him and comfort him, lest by any means such a one should be swallowed up with his excessive sorrow.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:8

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:8

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:8

text.en: Therefore I beg you to confirm your love toward him.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:9

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:9

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:9

text.en: For to this end I also wrote, that I might know the proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:10

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:10

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:10

text.en: Now I also forgive whomever you forgive anything. For if indeed I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven that one for your sakes in the presence of Christ,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:11

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:11

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:11

text.en: that no advantage may be gained over us by Satan, for we are not ignorant of his schemes.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:12

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:12

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:12

text.en: Now when I came to Troas for the Good News of Christ, and when a door was opened to me in the Lord,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:13

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:13

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:13

text.en: I had no relief for my spirit, because I didn’t find Titus my brother, but taking my leave of them, I went out into Macedonia.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:14

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:14

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:14

text.en: Now thanks be to God who always leads us in triumph in Christ, and reveals through us the sweet aroma of his knowledge in every place.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:15

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:15

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:15

text.en: For we are a sweet aroma of Christ to God in those who are being saved and in those who perish:

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:16

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:16

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:16

text.en: to the one a stench from death to death, to the other a sweet aroma from life to life. Who is sufficient for these things?

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:17

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:17

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 2:17

text.en: For we are not as so many, peddling the word of God. But as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God, we speak in Christ.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:1

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:1

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:1

text.en: Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as do some, letters of commendation to you or from you?

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:2

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:2

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:2

text.en: You are our letter, written in our hearts, known and read by all men,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:3

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:3

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:3

text.en: being revealed that you are a letter of Christ, served by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tablets of stone, but in tablets that are hearts of flesh.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:4

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:4

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:4

text.en: Such confidence we have through Christ toward God,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:5

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:5

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:5

text.en: not that we are sufficient of ourselves to account anything as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:6

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:6

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:6

text.en: who also made us sufficient as servants of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:7

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:7

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:7

text.en: But if the service of death, written engraved on stones, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly on the face of Moses for the glory of his face, which was passing away,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:8

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:8

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:8

text.en: won’t service of the Spirit be with much more glory?

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:9

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:9

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:9

text.en: For if the service of condemnation has glory, the service of righteousness exceeds much more in glory.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:10

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:10

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:10

text.en: For most certainly that which has been made glorious has not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasses.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:11

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:11

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 3:11

text.en: For if that which passes away was with glory, much more that which remains is in glory.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:1

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:1

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:1

text.en: Therefore, seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we don’t faint.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:2

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:2

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:2

text.en: But we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness nor handling the word of God deceitfully, but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:3

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:3

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:3

text.en: Even if our Good News is veiled, it is veiled in those who are dying,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:4

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:4

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:4

text.en: in whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, that the light of the Good News of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not dawn on them.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:5

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:5

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:5

text.en: For we don’t preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:6

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:6

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:6

text.en: seeing it is God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:13

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:13

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:13

text.en: But having the same spirit of faith, according to that which is written, “I believed, and therefore I spoke.” We also believe, and therefore we also speak,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:14

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:14

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:14

text.en: knowing that he who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also through Jesus, and will present us with you.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:15

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:15

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:15

text.en: For all things are for your sakes, that the grace, being multiplied through the many, may cause the thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:16

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:16

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:16

text.en: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:17

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:17

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:17

text.en: For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:18

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:18

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 4:18

text.en: while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:10

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:10

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:10

text.en: For we must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ that each one may receive the things in the body according to what he has done, whether good or bad.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:11

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:11

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:11

text.en: Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are revealed to God, and I hope that we are revealed also in your consciences.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:12

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:12

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:12

text.en: For we are not commending ourselves to you again, but speak as giving you occasion of boasting on our behalf, that you may have something to answer those who boast in appearance and not in heart.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:13

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:13

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:13

text.en: For if we are beside ourselves, it is for God. Or if we are of sober mind, it is for you.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:14

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:14

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:14

text.en: For the love of Christ compels us; because we judge thus: that one died for all, therefore all died.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:15

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:15

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:15

text.en: He died for all, that those who live should no longer live to themselves, but to him who for their sakes died and rose again.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:16

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:16

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:16

text.en: Therefore we know no one according to the flesh from now on. Even though we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him so no more.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:17

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:17

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:17

text.en: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:18

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:18

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:18

text.en: But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:19

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:19

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:19

text.en: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:20

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:20

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:20

text.en: We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:21

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:21

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 5:21

text.en: For him who knew no sin he made to be sin on our behalf, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:1

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:1

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:1

text.en: Having therefore these promises, beloved, let’s cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:2

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:2

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:2

text.en: Open your hearts to us. We wronged no one. We corrupted no one. We took advantage of no one.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:3

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:3

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:3

text.en: I say this not to condemn you, for I have said before that you are in our hearts to die together and live together.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:4

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:4

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:4

text.en: Great is my boldness of speech toward you. Great is my boasting on your behalf. I am filled with comfort. I overflow with joy in all our affliction.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:5

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:5

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:5

text.en: For even when we had come into Macedonia, our flesh had no relief, but we were afflicted on every side. Fightings were outside. Fear was inside.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:6

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:6

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:6

text.en: Nevertheless, he who comforts the lowly, God, comforted us by the coming of Titus,

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:7

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:7

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:7

text.en: and not by his coming only, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted in you while he told us of your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced still more.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:8

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:8

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:8

text.en: For though I grieved you with my letter, I do not regret it, though I did regret it. For I see that my letter made you grieve, though just for a while.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:9

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:9

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:9

text.en: I now rejoice, not that you were grieved, but that you were grieved to repentance. For you were grieved in a godly way, that you might suffer loss by us in nothing.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:10

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:10

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:10

text.en: For godly sorrow produces repentance leading to salvation, which brings no regret. But the sorrow of the world produces death.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:11

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:11

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:11

text.en: For behold, this same thing, that you were grieved in a godly way, what earnest care it worked in you. Yes, what defense, indignation, fear, longing, zeal, and vindication! In everything you demonstrated yourselves to be pure in the matter.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:12

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:12

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:12

text.en: So although I wrote to you, I wrote not for his cause that did the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered the wrong, but that your earnest care for us might be revealed in you in the sight of God.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:13

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:13

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:13

text.en: Therefore we have been comforted. In our comfort we rejoiced the more exceedingly for the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by you all.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:14

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:14

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:14

text.en: For if in anything I have boasted to him on your behalf, I was not disappointed. But as we spoke all things to you in truth, so our glorying also which I made before Titus was found to be truth.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:15

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:15

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:15

text.en: His affection is more abundantly toward you, while he remembers all of your obedience, how with fear and trembling you received him.

title.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:16

summary.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:16

speaker.en: Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 7:16

text.en: I rejoice that in everything I am confident concerning you.

title.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:10

summary.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:10

speaker.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:10

text.en: Therefore, brothers, be more diligent to make your calling and election sure. For if you do these things, you will never stumble.

title.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:11

summary.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:11

speaker.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:11

text.en: For thus you will be richly supplied with the entrance into the eternal Kingdom of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.

title.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:12

summary.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:12

speaker.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:12

text.en: Therefore I will not be negligent to remind you of these things, though you know them and are established in the present truth.

title.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:13

summary.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:13

speaker.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:13

text.en: I think it right, as long as I am in this tent, to stir you up by reminding you,

title.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:14

summary.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:14

speaker.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:14

text.en: knowing that the putting off of my tent comes swiftly, even as our Lord Jesus Christ made clear to me.

title.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:15

summary.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:15

speaker.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:15

text.en: Yes, I will make every effort that you may always be able to remember these things even after my departure.

title.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:16

summary.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:16

speaker.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:16

text.en: For we didn’t follow cunningly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty.

title.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:17

summary.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:17

speaker.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:17

text.en: For he received from God the Father honor and glory when the voice came to him from the Majestic Glory, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

title.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:18

summary.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:18

speaker.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:18

text.en: We heard this voice come out of heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain.

title.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:19

summary.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:19

speaker.en: Peter’s Second Letter 1:19

text.en: We have the more sure word of prophecy; and you do well that you heed it as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star arises in your hearts,

title.en: John 20:19

summary.en: John 20:19

speaker.en: John 20:19

text.en: When therefore it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the middle and said to them, “Peace be to you.”

title.en: John 20:20

summary.en: John 20:20

speaker.en: John 20:20

text.en: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord.

title.en: John 20:21

summary.en: John 20:21

speaker.en: John 20:21

text.en: Jesus therefore said to them again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”

title.en: John 20:22

summary.en: John 20:22

speaker.en: John 20:22

text.en: When he had said this, he breathed on them, and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit!

title.en: John 20:23

summary.en: John 20:23

speaker.en: John 20:23

text.en: If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven them. If you retain anyone’s sins, they have been retained.”

title.en: John 20:24

summary.en: John 20:24

speaker.en: John 20:24

text.en: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, wasn’t with them when Jesus came.

title.en: John 20:25

summary.en: John 20:25

speaker.en: John 20:25

text.en: The other disciples therefore said to him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.”

title.en: John 20:26

summary.en: John 20:26

speaker.en: John 20:26

text.en: After eight days, again his disciples were inside and Thomas was with them. Jesus came, the doors being locked, and stood in the middle, and said, “Peace be to you.”

title.en: John 20:27

summary.en: John 20:27

speaker.en: John 20:27

text.en: Then he said to Thomas, “Reach here your finger, and see my hands. Reach here your hand, and put it into my side. Don’t be unbelieving, but believing.”

title.en: John 20:28

summary.en: John 20:28

speaker.en: John 20:28

text.en: Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”

title.en: John 20:29

summary.en: John 20:29

speaker.en: John 20:29

text.en: Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.”

title.en: John 20:30

summary.en: John 20:30

speaker.en: John 20:30

text.en: Therefore Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book;

title.en: John 20:31

summary.en: John 20:31

speaker.en: John 20:31

text.en: but these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:1

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:1

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:1

text.en: After these things, Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. He revealed himself this way.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:2

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:2

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:2

text.en: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:3

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:3

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:3

text.en: Simon Peter said to them, “I’m going fishing.” They told him, “We are also coming with you.” They immediately went out and entered into the boat. That night, they caught nothing.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:4

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:4

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:4

text.en: But when day had already come, Jesus stood on the beach; yet the disciples didn’t know that it was Jesus.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:5

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:5

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:5

text.en: Jesus therefore said to them, “Children, have you anything to eat?” They answered him, “No.”

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:6

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:6

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:6

text.en: He said to them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” They cast it therefore, and now they weren’t able to draw it in for the multitude of fish.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:7

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:7

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:7

text.en: That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It’s the Lord!” So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he wrapped his coat around himself (for he was naked), and threw himself into the sea.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:8

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:8

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:8

text.en: But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away), dragging the net full of fish.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:9

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:9

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:9

text.en: So when they got out on the land, they saw a fire of coals there, with fish and bread laid on it.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:10

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:10

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:10

text.en: Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish which you have just caught.”

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:11

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:11

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:11

text.en: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land, full of one hundred fifty-three great fish. Even though there were so many, the net wasn’t torn.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:12

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:12

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:12

text.en: Jesus said to them, “Come and eat breakfast!” None of the disciples dared inquire of him, “Who are you?” knowing that it was the Lord.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:13

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:13

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:13

text.en: Then Jesus came and took the bread, gave it to them, and the fish likewise.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:14

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:14

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:14

text.en: This is now the third time that Jesus was revealed to his disciples after he had risen from the dead.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:15

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:15

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:15

text.en: So when they had eaten their breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.” He said to him, “Feed my lambs.”

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:16

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:16

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:16

text.en: He said to him again a second time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.” He said to him, “Tend my sheep.”

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:17

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:17

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:17

text.en: He said to him the third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you have affection for me?” Peter was grieved because he asked him the third time, “Do you have affection for me?” He said to him, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:18

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:18

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:18

text.en: Most certainly I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked where you wanted to. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will dress you and carry you where you don’t want to go.”

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:19

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:19

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:19

text.en: Now he said this, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God. When he had said this, he said to him, “Follow me.”

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:20

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:20

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:20

text.en: Then Peter, turning around, saw a disciple following. This was the disciple whom Jesus loved, the one who had also leaned on Jesus’ chest at the supper and asked, “Lord, who is going to betray you?”

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:21

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:21

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:21

text.en: Peter, seeing him, said to Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?”

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:22

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:22

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:22

text.en: Jesus said to him, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:23

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:23

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:23

text.en: This saying therefore went out among the brothers that this disciple wouldn’t die. Yet Jesus didn’t say to him that he wouldn’t die, but, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you?”

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:24

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:24

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:24

text.en: This is the disciple who testifies about these things, and wrote these things. We know that his witness is true.

title.en: The Good News According to John 21:25

summary.en: The Good News According to John 21:25

speaker.en: The Good News According to John 21:25

text.en: There are also many other things which Jesus did, which if they would all be written, I suppose that even the world itself wouldn’t have room for the books that would be written.

title.en: Matthew 14:22

summary.en: Matthew 14:22

speaker.en: Matthew 14:22

text.en: Immediately Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he sent the multitudes away.

title.en: Matthew 14:23

summary.en: Matthew 14:23

speaker.en: Matthew 14:23

text.en: After he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into the mountain by himself to pray. When evening had come, he was there alone.

title.en: Matthew 14:24

summary.en: Matthew 14:24

speaker.en: Matthew 14:24

text.en: But the boat was now in the middle of the sea, distressed by the waves, for the wind was contrary.

title.en: Matthew 14:25

summary.en: Matthew 14:25

speaker.en: Matthew 14:25

text.en: In the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came to them, walking on the sea.

title.en: Matthew 14:26

summary.en: Matthew 14:26

speaker.en: Matthew 14:26

text.en: When the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, “It’s a ghost!” and they cried out for fear.

title.en: Matthew 14:27

summary.en: Matthew 14:27

speaker.en: Matthew 14:27

text.en: But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, “Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.”

title.en: Matthew 14:28

summary.en: Matthew 14:28

speaker.en: Matthew 14:28

text.en: Peter answered him and said, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters.”

title.en: Matthew 14:29

summary.en: Matthew 14:29

speaker.en: Matthew 14:29

text.en: He said, “Come!” Peter stepped down from the boat and walked on the waters to come to Jesus.

title.en: Matthew 14:30

summary.en: Matthew 14:30

speaker.en: Matthew 14:30

text.en: But when he saw that the wind was strong, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, “Lord, save me!”

title.en: Matthew 14:31

summary.en: Matthew 14:31

speaker.en: Matthew 14:31

text.en: Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and said to him, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”

title.en: Matthew 14:32

summary.en: Matthew 14:32

speaker.en: Matthew 14:32

text.en: When they got up into the boat, the wind ceased.

title.en: Matthew 14:33

summary.en: Matthew 14:33

speaker.en: Matthew 14:33

text.en: Those who were in the boat came and worshiped him, saying, “You are truly the Son of God!”

title.en: Matthew 14:34

summary.en: Matthew 14:34

speaker.en: Matthew 14:34

text.en: When they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret.

title.en: Matthew 15:12

summary.en: Matthew 15:12

speaker.en: Matthew 15:12

text.en: Then the disciples came and said to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this saying?”

title.en: Matthew 15:13

summary.en: Matthew 15:13

speaker.en: Matthew 15:13

text.en: But he answered, “Every plant which my heavenly Father didn’t plant will be uprooted.

title.en: Matthew 15:14

summary.en: Matthew 15:14

speaker.en: Matthew 15:14

text.en: Leave them alone. They are blind guides of the blind. If the blind guide the blind, both will fall into a pit.”

title.en: Matthew 15:15

summary.en: Matthew 15:15

speaker.en: Matthew 15:15

text.en: Peter answered him, “Explain the parable to us.”

title.en: Matthew 15:16

summary.en: Matthew 15:16

speaker.en: Matthew 15:16

text.en: So Jesus said, “Do you also still not understand?

title.en: Matthew 15:17

summary.en: Matthew 15:17

speaker.en: Matthew 15:17

text.en: Don’t you understand that whatever goes into the mouth passes into the belly and then out of the body?

title.en: Matthew 15:18

summary.en: Matthew 15:18

speaker.en: Matthew 15:18

text.en: But the things which proceed out of the mouth come out of the heart, and they defile the man.

title.en: Matthew 15:19

summary.en: Matthew 15:19

speaker.en: Matthew 15:19

text.en: For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual sins, thefts, false testimony, and blasphemies.

title.en: Matthew 15:20

summary.en: Matthew 15:20

speaker.en: Matthew 15:20

text.en: These are the things which defile the man; but to eat with unwashed hands doesn’t defile the man.”

title.en: Matthew 15:21

summary.en: Matthew 15:21

speaker.en: Matthew 15:21

text.en: Jesus went out from there and withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon.

title.en: Matthew 15:32

summary.en: Matthew 15:32

speaker.en: Matthew 15:32

text.en: Jesus summoned his disciples and said, “I have compassion on the multitude, because they have continued with me now three days and have nothing to eat. I don’t want to send them away fasting, or they might faint on the way.”

title.en: Matthew 15:33

summary.en: Matthew 15:33

speaker.en: Matthew 15:33

text.en: The disciples said to him, “Where could we get so many loaves in a deserted place as to satisfy so great a multitude?”

title.en: Matthew 15:34

summary.en: Matthew 15:34

speaker.en: Matthew 15:34

text.en: Jesus said to them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven, and a few small fish.”

title.en: Matthew 15:35

summary.en: Matthew 15:35

speaker.en: Matthew 15:35

text.en: He commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground;

title.en: Matthew 15:36

summary.en: Matthew 15:36

speaker.en: Matthew 15:36

text.en: and he took the seven loaves and the fish. He gave thanks and broke them, and gave to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.

title.en: Matthew 15:37

summary.en: Matthew 15:37

speaker.en: Matthew 15:37

text.en: They all ate and were filled. They took up seven baskets full of the broken pieces that were left over.

title.en: Matthew 15:38

summary.en: Matthew 15:38

speaker.en: Matthew 15:38

text.en: Those who ate were four thousand men, in addition to women and children.

title.en: Matthew 15:39

summary.en: Matthew 15:39

speaker.en: Matthew 15:39

text.en: Then he sent away the multitudes, got into the boat, and came into the borders of Magdala.

title.en: The Good News According to Matthew 17:1

summary.en: The Good News According to Matthew 17:1

speaker.en: The Good News According to Matthew 17:1
